# What Sentry auth tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Two shapes are read. Three of the four kinds Sentry names carry thirty-two
# random bytes written as hexadecimal, which is sixty-four characters behind a
# seven character prefix; the organization token carries the base64 of a JSON
# payload, an underscore, and the base64 of thirty-two random bytes.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is, written out until each part is the length the pattern reads it
# at: sixty-four characters of hexadecimal body, thirty-two of organization
# payload — a multiple of base64's group — and forty-three of secret. None of
# the three is an abbreviation, since a part shortened for readability would
# leave a case holding no token at all.
#
# The block on the digest is not a token and nobody issued it. What it holds is
# a SHA-256 written behind a prefix, which is a hexadecimal body's shape
# exactly.

patterns: sentry-auth-token

# A token as it is written. The three kinds with a hexadecimal body differ only
# in the one character naming the kind, so what is below differs in where the
# token stands rather than in what it is allowed to do: the environment
# assignment sentry-cli reads it from, the bearer token header it is sent in,
# and the command line a release step passes it on.

case:     a user token in an environment assignment
in:       SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=«sentry-auth-token»

case:     a user token in a bearer token header
in:       Authorization: Bearer sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      Authorization: Bearer «sentry-auth-token»

case:     a user application token
in:       sntrya_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     an internal integration token
in:       sntryi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     an organization token on a command line
in:       sentry-cli --auth-token sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a releases new 1.0.0
out:      sentry-cli --auth-token «sentry-auth-token» releases new 1.0.0

case:     an organization token in the json that first reports it
in:       {"token":"sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a","name":"CI"}
out:      {"token":"«sentry-auth-token»","name":"CI"}

case:     an organization token in an environment assignment
in:       SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=«sentry-auth-token»

case:     a user token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:      the token is «sentry-auth-token».

case:     a user token between tabs
in:       \tsntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\t
out:      \t«sentry-auth-token»\t

case:     a user token before a crlf
in:       SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\r\n
out:      SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=«sentry-auth-token»\r\n

case:     a token in a markdown code span
in:       `sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef`
out:      `«sentry-auth-token»`

case:     a user token immediately against japanese on both sides
in:       トークンはsntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefです
out:      トークンは«sentry-auth-token»です

case:     a user token against an invalid byte
in:       \xffsntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\xff
out:      \xff«sentry-auth-token»\xff

case:     a token cut short with an ellipsis
in:       sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234...
out:      sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234...

# The character naming the kind, which is the one place the four prefixes
# differ. Four of them are read — u for a user token, a for a user application
# token, i for an internal integration token, s for an organization token — and
# a fifth character names no kind Sentry has.

case:     a kind the vendor's enumeration does not name
in:       sntryt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      sntryt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the vendor's name written in full, which carries an e the anchor does not
in:       sentry_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      sentry_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an uppercase anchor
in:       SNTRYU_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      SNTRYU_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries its separator
in:       sntryu-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      sntryu-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an uppercase kind character behind a lowercase opening
in:       sntryU_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      sntryU_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an uppercase organization kind
in:       sntryS_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      sntryS_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     the separator where the kind belongs
in:       sntry__0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      sntry__0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The hexadecimal body. It is thirty-two random bytes written two characters a
# byte, which is sixty-four, and the count is read exactly: a run longer than it
# is a token with something written after it, and only the token is redacted,
# while a body shorter than it — which is what a line cut to a column limit
# leaves — is no token at all and every random character before the cut comes
# through in the clear. Uppercase is not admitted, since the vendor writes none.

case:     a hexadecimal run longer than a body
in:       sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefa
out:      «sentry-auth-token»a

case:     a hexadecimal body one character short
in:       SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case:     a hexadecimal body written in uppercase
in:       sntryu_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      sntryu_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     a letter past f at the first character of a hexadecimal body
in:       sntryu_g123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      sntryu_g123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a user application token with a body one character short
in:       sntrya_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      sntrya_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case:     an internal integration token with a hexadecimal run one character longer than a body
in:       sntryi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefa
out:      «sentry-auth-token»a

case:     a token cut off at its prefix
in:       SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntryu_
out:      SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=sntryu_

# The organization token's two segments. The payload is base64 with its padding
# kept, so its length is a multiple of four and at most two of those characters
# are padding; the secret is base64 with its padding stripped, so it is the
# forty-three characters thirty-two bytes come to and carries none. The
# underscore between them belongs to neither alphabet, which is what ends the
# payload where it stands and what makes the count behind it readable at all.
#
# Two cases below carry no run of the file's own: a payload of one whole group
# of four is the ordered run's own opening, but the base64 of an actual payload
# object naming the organization and its urls is a body of one class alone that
# the ordered run cannot state, and the file's header says so.

case:     an organization token whose payload is one group of four
in:       sntrys_0123_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     an organization token whose payload closes with two padding characters and is otherwise a single group
in:       sntrys_01==_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     an organization token whose payload is the base64 of a payload object
in:       sntrys_eyJpYXQiOjE3MDAwMDAwMDAsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vc2VudHJ5LmlvIiwicmVnaW9uX3VybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vdXMuc2VudHJ5LmlvIiwib3JnIjoiYWNtZSJ9_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     an organization payload closing with one padding character
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde=_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     an organization payload closing with two
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd==_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     an organization payload closing with three, which base64 never calls for
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abc===_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abc===_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     an organization payload that is not a multiple of base64's group
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     an organization token with no payload
in:       sntrys__0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      sntrys__0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     an organization secret one character short
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789
out:      sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789

case:     a base64 run longer than an organization secret
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «sentry-auth-token»b

case:     padding where an organization secret ends
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789=
out:      sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789=

case:     a third underscore inside an organization secret
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd_f0123456789a
out:      sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd_f0123456789a

case:     no separator between the two segments
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab

case:     a hyphen at the first character of an organization secret
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_-123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_-123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     padding written after a whole organization token
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a=
out:      «sentry-auth-token»=

# What a token may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of a
# match, as there is none in any built-in but the Slack and Stripe ones: a
# demand in front would drop a token written against a letter rather than trim
# it, and one behind would drop a token with a character of its own alphabet
# after it.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN_sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN_«sentry-auth-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xsntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      x«sentry-auth-token»

case:     a token inside quotes
in:       export SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN="sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
out:      export SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN="«sentry-auth-token»"

case:     a token before a hyphenated word
in:       sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-suffix
out:      «sentry-auth-token»-suffix

# Two tokens written together. The alphabet an organization token's segments are
# written in holds every letter the anchor is written in and every character
# naming a kind, and the separator a prefix closes with is the one such a token
# already carries between its segments, so a payload closing with sntrys or
# sntryu opens a candidate whose own body begins where the first token's secret
# does. The two spans overlap and are redacted as one, which is what a scan
# resuming past a match would have stepped over.

case:     two tokens separated by a space
in:       sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sentry-auth-token» «sentry-auth-token»

case:     a token written straight onto the end of another
in:       sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «sentry-auth-token»«sentry-auth-token»

case:     an organization token beginning inside the payload of another
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789ab_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     a user token beginning inside the payload of an organization token
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     two organization tokens with nothing between them
in:       sntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789asntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «sentry-auth-token»«sentry-auth-token»

case:     an organization token immediately against japanese on both sides
in:       トークンはsntrys_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789aです
out:      トークンは«sentry-auth-token»です

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. A hexadecimal body is thirty-two
# random bytes written in hexadecimal, which is a SHA-256 digest's shape
# exactly, so a digest written behind one of the three prefixes is redacted.
#
# That is the answer rather than a fault in it: such a run is a token's format
# exactly, so declining it would decline every token Sentry happened to write in
# the digits and the letters through f alone. What keeps it rare is the seven
# characters in front, which no digest carries. A SHA-1 is twenty-four short of
# the count and is left alone, and so is a digest written behind a hyphen.

case:     a sha-256 behind a prefix
in:       sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «sentry-auth-token»

case:     a sha-1 behind a prefix, which is short of the count
in:       sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sntryu_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a sha-256 behind a hyphen
in:       sntryu-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      sntryu-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The format Sentry minted before it
# prefixed its tokens is the same thirty-two random bytes with nothing in front
# of them, which is a SHA-256's shape with no anchor to narrow it by, so it is
# not read at all; a base64 payload carries no underscore and so hands the
# letters of the anchor nowhere to close however long it runs; no word of prose
# is spelled sntry with an underscore two characters behind it; and a JWT's
# segments are base64url where these are base64.

case:     a token of the format that carried no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a base64 payload carrying the letters of the anchor
in:       payload=sntryu0123456789abcdef0123456789sntrys0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      payload=sntryu0123456789abcdef0123456789sntrys0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a jwt
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef

case:     a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="uploading source maps" url=https://sentry.io/api/0/organizations/acme/releases/
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="uploading source maps" url=https://sentry.io/api/0/organizations/acme/releases/
